features.title: Object clipboard
features.scope: Copy/Cut/Paste and Paste in Place transfer objects, dependent symbols, timelines and scripts; linked symbols include their project-source snapshot, program-reachable linkage-only exports and transitive dependencies, and reject conflicts before mutation. Native key/paste input is applied once per payload, including interleaved input and custom shortcuts, with one Undo for each paste. Inline Stage text editing preserves mixed `TextFormatRun` spans across rich Copy/Cut/Paste (including across document tab switches) with plain-text OS clipboard fallback; on macOS Apple Silicon, cached formatting is tied to the system clipboard write, so equal-text replacements or unavailable ownership metadata use the destination text style. Script/code editors retain ordinary text paste. Complete resource snapshots transfer with remapped identities, exact content reuse and atomic path-conflict rejection. Native Figma clipboard payloads (`<!--(figma)...(/figma)-->` Deflate/Zstandard `fig-kiwi` scene graphs, excluding `Internal Only Canvas`), Figma `Copy as SVG` markup, SVG clipboard text and native bitmap clipboard data paste 1:1 onto the Stage (`⌘V` centered, `⌘⇧V` `Paste in Place` at document coordinates or normalized onto Stage for off-stage infinite-canvas origins) as editable vectors, strokes, gradients, cropped bitmap fills, editable text, masks, filters and collision-free `MovieClip` symbols in one Undo step. Native Adobe Illustrator, PDF 1.4–1.7 (`/XRef` + `/ObjStm`, `/ArtBox` selection bounds, CMYK/Gray/Separation/ICCBased colors, compound NonZero/EvenOdd holes, Type 2/3 `/Shading` + `/Pattern` multi-stop gradients, `W`/`W*` clipping masks, `/ExtGState` alpha/blend modes, `/Subtype /Form` nested symbols, `/SMask` bitmaps, and `/ToUnicode` `BT..ET` text) and PostScript Level 3 / AICB EPS clipboard flavors (`com.adobe.pdf`, `com.adobe.encapsulated-postscript`, `public.svg-image`) paste 1:1 onto Stage (`⌘V` centered, `⌘⇧V` Paste in Place, `Edit in Place` StageMapping, 1-Undo), while Stage Copy/Cut writes a single-generation multi-flavor pasteboard (`app.neoflash.stage-clipboard`, selection-cropped `/ArtBox` `com.adobe.pdf`, `com.adobe.encapsulated-postscript`, `public.svg-image`, and `<svg><!--(neoflash)...(/neoflash)-->` text) for 1:1 outbound paste into Illustrator, Figma and SVG tools with lossless NeoFlash round-trip.
features.limitations: Native acceptance of the new linked-source/resource/frame transfer remains pending. The 8 MiB clipboard cap rejects oversized snapshots explicitly. Exotic Illustrator live meshes, 3D effects or proprietary private AICB plugin streams outside PDF 1.7 / Level 3 PostScript approximate or emit Output warnings; clipboard flavor decoding enforces 8 MiB NeoFlash JSON and cumulative 64 MiB / 32,768-command / 4096x4096 vector-raster caps. Independent c39a29e acceptance (RESOURCES-HTML5-20261027T0323Z) covers the precise embedded/HTTP and pending-request observations in VERIFICATION.md; native resource authoring and full network semantics remain unverified.

features.title: Library and nested editing
features.scope: Reusable instances and nested editing preserve authored identity and scripts. Edit in place resolves one exact visible placement, composes its invertible affine transform through nested levels (including arbitrary oblique/skewed, rotated and negative-determinant reflected parent chains via SVD hit-testing, reversed mesh winding and affine gizmo mapping for Free Transform Envelope/Perspective, Asset Warp, IK, 3D, registration markers, bitmaps and filters), dims the frozen parent context and inverse-maps rendering, picking, selection, transforms, vector tools, drops, snapping and motion overlays; clean isolated definition editing remains a separate route. The session restores each level's playhead, active layer, selection, zoom/pan, ruler zero, frame range and Timeline focus, including paused independent-clip frames. A double-click on genuinely empty canvas with no active draft/gesture consumes the full press/release gesture and leaves exactly one hierarchy level without changing the sticky tool or immediately reopening the restored child; repeating the gesture continues upward. Entering a MovieClip by double-click requires an actual hit on that placement. Breadcrumbs retain direct navigation. Convert to Symbol offers aligned name/type/folder, exact nine-point registration without single-object double-offsetting, and export identifier/existing-class fields; the entered Name seeds the Identifier until it is edited explicitly while leaving Stage `<Instance Name>` empty by default on conversion and Library placement. Empty `SymbolInstance`s render an authoring-only `○+` Stage marker (clickable, marquee/Lasso-selectable, draggable and double-clickable for Edit in Place across Selection, Subselection and Free Transform) and report `0 × 0` `W`/`H` bounds, while selected instances paint a `+` registration crosshair at `(0, 0)`. The Library shows a real first-frame preview, persistent folders, inline and drag-and-drop folder/symbol organization (`drag_drop_symbol_to_folder`, `drag_drop_folder_to_folder`), search by name/path/linkage/class, Name/Type/Linkage sorting and visible linkage, plus Select unused items, Delete unused items, bulk folder moves and bulk symbol-type changes in one Undo step. Duplicate symbol clones non-scene symbols with fresh IDs and cleared linkage (including Stage context-menu `Duplicate symbol…` and Properties `Duplicate…` on a selected instance); Delete symbol removes the symbol and cleans up any placed instances across timelines in one Undo step; Swap symbol in the Library, Stage context-menu `Swap symbol…`, Properties `Swap…` symbol-picker popover or holding ⌥ (Alt) while dragging a symbol from the Library onto the Stage or a Timeline layer row/frame span replaces the symbol on the selected stage instance or active/hovered layer across its keyframes while preserving transform, name, scripts, filters, blend mode and compatible playback. Selected symbol-instance Properties also exposes per-instance behavior switching (`Movie Clip` / `Button` / `Graphic` stored in format-14 `Element.instance_behavior`, JSFL `element.symbolType` and XFL/SWF round-trips without mutating `Symbol.kind` in the Library), `Edit symbol`, `Position and size` (`X`/`Y`, `W`/`H` + `Constrain instance proportions`, `Scale X`/`Scale Y`, `Rotation`/`Skew`), `Colour effect` (`Style: None / Brightness / Tint / Advanced / Alpha`), `Display` and `Filters`, and `Break Apart` (`⌘B` or Stage context menu) expands a MovieClip, Button or Graphic instance into the evaluated child elements, groups and bitmap fills of its visible layers at the current frame. Symbols also support 9-slice scaling grids (`Scale9Mapping`, keeping the 4 corner regions unstretched while scaling edge and centre regions inversely to the instance's `scale_x`/`scale_y`, with interactive Stage 9-slice guide dragging, live clamping, `Escape` cancellation and 1-Undo) and portable Shared Library linkage (`SharedLibraryLinkage` in `library/shared_libraries.json`, `set_symbol_shared_library`, `sync_shared_library`, and external `.nflash` donor selection via the file chooser). Folder paths survive symbol clipboard transfers; conflicts reject before mutation. Empty symbol creation opens nested editing. Buttons expose Up/Over/Down/Hit, instance actions and authored/export-linked SimpleButton typing. Library Properties changes kind across references while preserving keys/scripts and refusing incompatible class linkage.
features.limitations: Edit in place refuses singular/non-finite transforms and non-affine 9-slice scaling instead of mutating geometry in the wrong coordinate space. Local guides and grid paint and snap on non-reflected axis-aligned and quarter-turn placements. Oblique and reflected placements omit local guides and grid. The local ruler requires both mapped axes to advance in positive screen directions. Other placements use screen units (R-063). Dedicated ⌥-drag replacement badges wait for NF2 request R-041. Arbitrary runtime state-object assignment and empty SimpleButton construction remain unsupported. Multi-object conversion requires a contiguous stack on one layer. Preview is the first frame. Resource files remain outside the symbol-folder tree.

features.title: Authored text
features.scope: The Stage Text tool creates point text on click and a fixed, multiline wrapping TextBox on drag. Editable authored TextBox supports logical dimensions, installed regular/bold/italic fonts, size/color/leading, left/center/right/justify alignment, per-range rich-text `TextFormatRun` persistence, HTML/CSS authoring (`set_selected_text_html` / `selected_text_to_html`), authored dynamic/input field options (`AuthoredTextFieldOptions`: `field_type`, `selectable`, `editable`, `border`, `background`, `password`, `max_chars`, `restrict`, `html`, `condense_white`, `auto_size`), `set_selected_text_auto_size` (`"none"`, `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"` resizing and anchoring in one Undo step) and conversion through characters to editable installed-font glyph contours. Selected TextBox Properties uses a compact classic Flash two-column inspector: `Text type` (`Static Text` / `Dynamic Text` / `Input Text`) and `Family` on one row; `Style` (`Regular` / `Bold` / `Italic` / `Bold Italic`), `Embed font` and `Embedding…` on one row (opening the existing NF2 dialog on the exact selected Family/Style, saving ranges/custom characters and committing the font resource plus field setting as one Undo step); `Size` (`pt`) and `Letter spacing` (`px`) on one row; `Color` and `Auto kern` on one row; compact `Selectable` / `HTML` / `Border` / `Underline` switches; `Paragraph` with 4-mode `Segmented` alignment, two-column `Indent` + `Line` spacing, two-column `Left` + `Right` margins and `Behavior` (`Single line` / `Multiline` / `Multiline no wrap` / `Password`); and collapsible `Options` (`URL`, two-column `Target` + `Max chars`, two-column `Variable` + `Restrict`). features.title: Frame-range operations
features.scope: An ordinary click selects one frame; Shift-click and pointer drag create exact rectangular layer/frame ranges, while hovering Timeline grid cells stays silent without tooltip clutter and preserves Grab keyframe cursors. Copy, cut, paste, move, clear, insert and remove time are atomic Undo operations. Left- or right-clicking blank Layers-column space below the rows deselects all layers (`layers_deselected`) and right-clicking opens the compact 10-item contextless layer menu (`Add new layer`, `Add new folder`, `Add motion guide` | `Paste layers` | `Show all`, `Clear all solo`, `Unlock all`, `Show all as solid` | `Expand all folders`, `Collapse all folders`). Right-clicking a selected frame preserves the chosen range, applies Remove Frames to it with Undo/Redo, and groups the six frame utility actions under a compact Utils submenu while Include frame scripts is exposed in Frame Properties. Range edits splitting cubic-representable tweens (`Linear`, `EaseIn`, `EaseOut`, `EaseInOut`, `Flash` and `CubicBezier`, including motion `property_eases`) subdivide editable `CubicBezier` sub-curves via De Casteljau subdivision instead of integer-frame pose baking. Explicit Include frame scripts transfers each selected layer-owned script once and rejects destination collisions; object scripts travel with placements. Independent layer ends can be set numerically or dragged and stop exposure in native and HTML5 evaluation. Range clipboard works within and across open document tabs, preserving visible layer order, stable animation identities and transitive symbols/resources/fonts/swatches/styles while remapping collisions. Edit multiple frames renders every keyframe in the onion range opaque, allows selecting objects that exist only on neighbouring keyframes, and applies Move, Resize, Scale, Rotate and Skew across all keyframes in the range in one Undo step. Pasting a multi-layer range creates missing destination layers in the same Undo transaction.
features.limitations: Paste creates missing destination layers and validates the complete candidate before committing. Trimming deletes later keys with Undo recovery. Range cuts through analytical Bounce/Elastic presets or guided motion spans fall back to frame-accurate pose keyframes, and reversing a motion tween turns its ◆ poses into classic keyframes. Edit multiple frames applies selection and transform gestures across the onion range; drawing and path-point reshape edits still target the current keyframe. Group requires members on the current keyframe and diagnoses selections that exist only on other frames. Reverse mirrors keyframe positions and time-inverts tween easing curves (baking spatial motion curves and one-way Bounce/Elastic spans into frame-accurate keyframes).

features.title: Timeline lifecycle and scene playback
features.scope: Phased Rust/WASM and HTML5 lifecycle ordering (ENTER_FRAME -> timeline step -> Construct / deepest-child-first REMOVED & REMOVED_FROM_STAGE -> FRAME_CONSTRUCTED -> Event.FRAME_LABEL / FrameScripts -> EXIT_FRAME -> RENDER): parent super() constructs timeline children, assigns typed slots and fires child ADDED before post-super() statements; synchronous AS3 goto*/nextFrame/prevFrame/*Scene supersede stale pending scripts via visit_id while preserving deferred AS2 goto semantics and detached-clip lifecycle events. Removing and recreating an instance starts a new lifetime; same-path symbol replacement resets subtree overrides, custom fields and clocks, invalidates old proxies and preserves siblings; accepted in Chrome/in-app HTML5. Scenes flatten in play order for Test Movie and HTML5 export (preserving scene-local timing for synchronized layers), while Control ▸ Test scene (⌥⌘↵) publishes and previews only the currently edited scene. Native Play all scenes with Loop off plays through the final scene before stopping. One-frame clips retain their initial visit while child clocks and EnterFrame continue. Late EXIT_FRAME initialization survives scope completion. Reentrant constructors and removal handlers preserve pending sibling callbacks and last frame metadata; direct Stage children retain captured event routes.
features.limitations: Reentrant AS3 navigation is bounded to 128 nested scopes and 4,096 lifecycle steps. Bulk removal notifications follow an atomic graph change; native per-child callback timing and complete historical Flash edge-case conformance remain outside the verified profile.

features.title: Shared Rust/WASM core
features.scope: The browser uses the same timeline runtime; tests call the actual compiled WASM. Runtime-created object identity, hierarchy, solid drawing, transformed bounds/hits and captured lifecycle routes use the shared Rust/WASM scene while authored documents remain immutable. Explicit linked MovieClip namespaces reuse the shared timeline evaluator with independent frame scripts, nested clocks and ref-based semantic targets, including detached playback. Bounded AMF0/AMF3 values are encoded/decoded in Rust and used by ByteArray object records and local AS2/AS3 SharedObject persistence. AS3 Array prototype borrowing (`Array.prototype.*`), unbound `toString`/`toLocaleString`, and sparse hole semantics share the runtime collection kernel (`T-011`). The second bounded runtime batch adds Rust date/number formatting, four rendered filter families and manual AS3 event payload classes. Published AS2 and AS3 movies on independent origins exchange SharedObject changes and messages through a self-hosted WebSocket relay. The relay sends late joiners the current state and optionally persists rooms across restarts.
features.limitations: A shared implementation does not prove compatibility with Flash behavior. The combined dynamic-display browser workflow and Restart passed; authored/dynamic reordering and full Flash construction order remain bounded. Independent 2b5deff evidence covers only the exact dynamic drawing/identity or binary packet scenarios in VERIFICATION.md; other members and native error/coercion fidelity remain unverified. Independent 798e28b evidence (LINKED-INTERFACES-HTML5-20261027T0243Z) applies only to the linked timeline and interface/accessor observations in VERIFICATION.md. AS2 host-error catch recovery, complete construction order and uncalled members remain unverified or outside the supported profile. Typed aliases, XML/XMLDocument, sparse indices and native AMF0/AMF3 `.sol` byte exchange work through Rust/WASM, with actual browser file-input/download and reload coverage. Vector, Dictionary, XMLList, IExternalizable, complete historical alias semantics, automatic Flash-storage discovery and native Adobe FMS/RTMP interoperability remain unsupported. SOL envelopes have no object identity and trailing array holes may disappear. Browser quota/access and HTTP(S) origin rules apply; Restart discards unflushed edits. AMF payload size excludes the storage envelope and historical filesystem overhead.

features.limitations: Extensions run strictly over the bounded `CommandStep` vocabulary inside the in-memory project transaction; arbitrary native dylibs, filesystem/network access and third-party package registries are outside scope. Interface localization covers the core catalog keys with deterministic `en-US` fallback; locked NF2 panel layouts keep their canonical design labels. AI connections require user-configured API keys (or a local OpenAI-compatible server), enforce HTTPS for cloud providers, expose no autonomous document-mutation, shell or filesystem tools, and apply proposed edits only when the author explicitly clicks `Apply` (`1` Undo step). Headless `jsfl` denies all `FLfile` reads, writes and deletes unless explicit `--allow-read`, `--allow-write` or `--allow-delete` capabilities are passed for canonical directory roots. Headless filesystem rollback covers returned errors, cooperative cancellation and failed response writes while the process remains alive; `SIGKILL`, process crashes and power loss cannot run the in-memory journal and have no persistent recovery log.

features.title: Editor accessibility and overall verification
features.scope: Authored and runtime accessibility metadata share live placement identity in Canvas and DOM publication, including role/name/description/shortcut/live attributes, native keyboard controls, Stage focus events and cleanup. Disabled, hidden, silent and retired controls leave the appropriate focus/semantic paths. Canvas supports authored reading order; DOM preserves its rendered hierarchy. Keyboard focus is visible on tool buttons, Library items, Timeline layers and Swatches cells. F1 search contains Tab and Shift+Tab and exposes its selected result while typing, and notifications expose complete polite Status or assertive Alert announcements without taking focus. In the native macOS desktop editor, `accessibility_bridge` exposes live `AccessKit` (`NSAccessibility`) semantic trees and action handlers (`Focus`, `Click`, `Increment`/`Decrement`/`SetValue`, `Expand`/`Collapse`) across Stage interactive/text/media elements (with window-space bounds, `Edit in Place` mapping, `tab_index` order, `silent` exclusion and `force_simple` child suppression), Timeline (`Role::Slider` playhead with unshadowed numeric frame values, `Role::Tree` layer rows and viewport-bounded `Role::Grid`/`Role::Cell` keyframe spans), and Library (`Role::Tree` folders, symbols and resources), while HTML5 `AccessibilityImplementation` bridges MSAA roles/states, `getChildIDArray()`/`accLocation()` child bounds and `accDoDefaultAction()`/`accSelect()` into the live DOM semantic overlay. Focused gradient stops can be moved, added and deleted by keyboard. Keyboard focus also identifies History and other menu rows, Actions tabs and pins and shortcut assignments. Tab traversal scrolls offscreen Properties, Actions and Motion Editor controls into view. Esc followed by Tab or Shift+Tab leaves the script text without editing it.
features.limitations: Live physical macOS VoiceOver spoken announcements remain unverified. DOM browse order is not independently reordered and raster-island semantics remain bounded.
